Thanks for the flag, Avery. I reviewed the redlines and attached comparison. High-level recommendations and proposed language below.

1) EU-only hosting obligation
- Position: We can accept an EU-region hosting commitment for the Order Form for Dedicated or Private deployments provided we: (a) include limited operational failover carve-outs for short-duration emergencies (e.g., disaster recovery) and (b) preserve our right to run services for maintenance/failover.
- Proposed Order Form clause (suggested):
  "Hosting Regions: Provider will host Customer Data in EU regions (EU). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider may (i) temporarily process Customer Data outside the EU for disaster recovery or maintenance for no more than 72 contiguous hours per calendar event, and (ii) route traffic to non-EU regions for capacity bursting where Customer has been notified and has provided prior written consent. Provider will ensure EU data residency under normal operations."

2) SCCs + Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA)
- Position: We accept executing the EU SCCs. For the TIA, we have a standard Transfer Addendum template we prefer; if the customer insists on their TIA, we can accept it only after an engineering/security review and limited representations.
- Ask: We should not sign bespoke TIAs that impose operational constraints (e.g., permanent prohibition on failover). Offer: sign Customer TIA with an addendum stating any operational exceptions (see Hosting Regions clause).

3) KMS / Customer-managed keys
- Position: We support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated offerings; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) roadmap but cannot guarantee full key separation for multi-tenant hosted.
- Proposed DPA language (suggested):
  "Key Management: For Dedicated and Private deployments, Provider will enable customer-managed keys (CMK) integration with customer KMS where feasible. For Hosted deployments, Provider offers envelope encryption and will evaluate BYOK options; any CMK commitments will be documented in a separate Security Addendum and subject to operational onboarding."

4) Processor / Subprocessor mapping
- Position: Provide a current list of subprocessors and commit to 30 days notice for new processors. For contractual clarity, include a DPA exhibit listing subprocessors and roles (controller/processor mapping).
- Proposed DPA exhibit entry (suggested):
  "Subprocessor Roster: Provider maintains a roster of subprocessors and their roles. Provider will provide Customer with the current roster upon execution and notify Customer of any additions 30 days prior to engagement."

Next steps I recommend:
- Avery/Ben: confirm commercial appetite for the Hosting Regions clause above (trade-offs: we limit failover flexibility).
- Avery: send Marta the three discrete options for the TIA (Customer TIA, Redwood TIA, or Redwood TIA + operational carve-outs) and ask which they prefer.
- Engineering/Security review (I will copy the security team if customer chooses own TIA).

I'll attach the suggested redlines in a short doc for direct copy/paste. If we need escalation on the EU-only ask, flag and I can loop in Head of Legal.

Hi Marta / Tom — thanks for sending the redlines and for the quick sync today. Per Laura's review above, here's a concise set of options and a proposed timeline so we can align and get to signature by 11/10 if possible.

Summary of options (pick one):
1) Standard route (fastest): Redwood executes EU SCCs + Redwood Transfer Addendum (our standard TIA). We accept an "EU regions by default" hosting commitment with the emergency failover carve-out and 72-hour limit. No bespoke TIA.
2) Customer TIA (preferred by KiteLabs): Redwood will review and, subject to a security/engineering review, accept Customer TIA with operational carve-outs identical to the Hosting Regions clause. This path requires an additional security review step (~5 business days).
3) Dedicated/Private-only concession: For Dedicated or Private, we can accept stronger residency guarantees and CMK support documented in a Security Addendum, but require explicit acceptance that maintenance/failover may be outside EU as described.

Requested action from KiteLabs by EOD Mon 02/11:
- Confirm which option you prefer (1, 2 or 3).
- Confirm whether you want customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private and provide KMS vendor details if yes.

Attachments: proposed_redlines_orderform_kitelabs.docx (copy/paste-friendly excerpts), DPA_SCCs_Comparison.xlsx

If we get confirmation on Option 1 today we can lock the commercial terms and circulate DocuSign for signature by 11/03. If you choose Option 2, please share the TIA for our security review; that will push the timeline ~5 business days.
